\multicolumn{6}{@{}l@{}}{\textbf{V13}\enspace\textit{Raw or Poisson-denoised within-type covariance in the bulk}} \\*
\texttt{V13a} & Bulk covariance under cell-depth sampling then scaling, $a^2\sum_j m_j(\bm\Sigma^{\mathrm{bio}}_j+\operatorname{diag}\bm\mu_j)$, against bulk-depth sampling, $a^2\sum_j m_j\bm\Sigma^{\mathrm{bio}}_j+a\operatorname{diag}(\sum_j m_j\bm\mu_j)$; binomial thinning equals bulk-depth sampling & Poisson and binomial MGFs summed from the pmf; generic third-order CGF per type, $G=J=2$; Hessian of the pooled CGF at $0$; thinning and bulk-depth sampling have the same CGF & exact & {pass} & 744 \\
\texttt{V13b} & With $m_j=np_j$: $\operatorname{Cov}\bm y=\phi\,\bm S^{\mathrm{bio}}(\bm p)+c\operatorname{diag}(\tilde{\bm\mu}\bm p)=\phi\{\bm S^{\mathrm{bio}}(\bm p)+a^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tilde{\bm\mu}\bm p)\}$; the raw plug-in $\phi\,\bm S^{\mathrm{raw}}(\bm p)$ is exact iff $a=1$; the denoised one only as $a\to\infty$; sampling exceeds biology for gene $g$ iff $\tilde\mu_g(\bm p)>a S^{\mathrm{bio}}_{gg}(\bm p)$ & raw minus bulk-depth covariance: $an(a-1)(\tilde{\bm\mu}\bm p)_g$ on the diagonal, $0$ off it; its root in $a$ is $1$; limit of $\operatorname{Cov}\bm y/\phi-\bm S^{\mathrm{bio}}$ as $a\to\infty$ is $0$ & exact & {pass} & 748, 802 \\

\multicolumn{6}{@{}l@{}}{\textbf{V14}\enspace\textit{Denoised within-type covariance: technical size factor and finite-sample bias}} \\*

\texttt{V14b} & eq-count-covariance, and the population version of eq-denoised-within equals the target $\operatorname{Cov}(\bm B s^{\mathrm{bio}}\bm\lambda)=\bm B[(1+\nu^{\mathrm{bio}})\bm\Sigma^\lambda+\nu^{\mathrm{bio}}\bm\mu\bm\mu^{\mathsf T}]\bm B$ & Poisson moments from the pmf; tower rule over $(s,\bm\lambda)$, $G=2$, gene-wise capture $\bm B$; $\bm V\to\operatorname{Cov}\bm x$, $\bar{\bm x}\to\mathbb E\bm x$ gives the target exactly & exact & {pass} & 763 \\

Deviation: the printed form is consistent, biased at order $1/C_j$; corrected in 05-1 & exact & \textbf{flag} & 763 \\
\texttt{V14d} & Plugging the total extrinsic noise $\nu$ (a size factor carrying $s^{\mathrm{bio}}$ and $s^{\mathrm{tech}}$) for $\nu^{\mathrm{tech}}$ returns $\bm B\bm\Sigma^\lambda\bm B$ and drops $\nu^{\mathrm{bio}}\bm B(\bm\Sigma^\lambda+\bm\mu\bm\mu^{\mathsf T})\bm B$ & population estimator with $\kappa=\nu/(1+\nu)$, $\nu$ from V14a; difference from the target factorised & exact & {pass} & 766, 800 \\

\multicolumn{6}{@{}l@{}}{\textbf{V15}\enspace\textit{Gaussian transport map (Bisque's gene-wise map as its diagonal case)}} \\*

\multicolumn{6}{@{}l@{}}{\textbf{V16}\enspace\textit{Bulk sampling diagonal against the variance scale: identifiability and profile}} \\*
\texttt{V16a} & Covariance alone, given $\bm p$: $(\phi,k)\mapsto\phi\,\bm S^{\mathrm{bio}}(\bm p)+k\operatorname{diag}(\tilde{\bm\mu}\bm p)$ is identifiable iff $\bm S^{\mathrm{bio}}(\bm p)$ is not a multiple of $\operatorname{diag}(\tilde{\bm\mu}\bm p)$ & Jacobian $[\operatorname{vec}\bm S,\operatorname{vec}\bm D]$: all $2\times2$ minors vanish iff $\bm S=\kappa\bm D$ ($G=2,3$, generic symmetric $\bm S$); $\bm S=\bm D/2$, $\bm m=(2,3)$: $(\phi,k)=(4,6)$ and $(8,4)$ give $\operatorname{diag}(16,24)$; Fisher determinant $0$ there, $\frac{7}{678976}$ for a non-proportional $\bm S$ & exact & {pass} & qmd \\
\texttt{V16b} & With the mean $c\,\tilde{\bm\mu}\bm p$ of the article and $\operatorname{Cov}\bm y=\phi\,\bm S^{\mathrm{bio}}(\bm p)+c\operatorname{diag}(\tilde{\bm\mu}\bm p)$, $(c,\phi)$, and so $(\phi,a)$, is identified whenever $\bm S^{\mathrm{bio}}(\bm p)\neq\bm 0$, also when it is a multiple of the diagonal & Fisher information of $(c,\phi)$ from the expected Hessian, $G=2$: $\bm I=\bm I_{\mathrm{cov}}+\operatorname{diag}(\bm m^\top\bm\Sigma^{-1}\bm m,0)$, $\det\bm I=(\bm m^\top\bm\Sigma^{-1}\bm m)I_{\phi\phi}+\det\bm I_{\mathrm{cov}}$; at $\bm S=\kappa\bm D$: $\det\bm I_{\mathrm{cov}}=0$, $\det\bm I=\frac{\kappa^{2} \left(m_{1} + m_{2}\right)}{\left(c + \kappa \phi\right)^{3}}$; $\partial(c,\phi)/\partial(\phi,a)$ has determinant $\phi/a^2$ & exact & {pass} & qmd \\
\texttt{V16c} & Cost: with $\phi=ac$ and $\bm M=a\bm S^{\mathrm{bio}}(\bm p)+\operatorname{diag}(\tilde{\bm\mu}\bm p)$, $\hat c$ for fixed $(\bm p,a)$ is the positive root of $Cc^2+Gc-A=0$; $a$ needs a one-dimensional numerical profile; without the diagonal, $\hat c$ is the GLS scale and $\hat\phi=Q/G$ & $2c^2\,\partial_c\ell=A-Gc-Cc^2$, $A=\bm y^\top\bm M^{-1}\bm y$, $C=\bm m^\top\bm M^{-1}\bm m$ ($G=2$, generic $\bm M$); one positive root; $\partial_c^2\ell=-G/(2c^2)-C/c<0$ there & exact & {pass} & qmd \\

\addlinespace[4pt]
\multicolumn{6}{@{}l@{}}{\textbf{V18}\enspace\textit{D-, E- and A-optimal gene panels from the Fisher information for $\bm p$}} \\*
\texttt{V18a} & With a common within-type covariance, $\bm S_W(\bm p)=\bSigma_W$ and the information for the free coordinates $\bm\theta$ ($\bm p=\bm p_0+\bm K\bm\theta$) is $n_i\bm K\T\bm M\T\bSigma_W^{-1}\bm M\bm K$; for $J=2$ it is $n_i\bm\Delta\T\bSigma_W^{-1}\bm\Delta$ & Expected negative Hessian of the Gaussian log-likelihood, $G=2$, $J=3$, generic $\bm M$ and $\bSigma_W$; Hessian free of $\bm y$; $n_i=c^2/\phi$ & exact & {pass} & qmd \\

\multicolumn{6}{@{}l@{}}{\textbf{V20}\enspace\textit{Negative-binomial counts are sub-exponential: moments, Chernoff and Bernstein range bounds}} \\*
